gen-silkscreen-gf-noto-sans-nko-unjoined: Silkscreen spaces its blocky, lo-fi letters so far apart you can almost feel the gaps, while Noto Sans NKo Unjoined keeps small letters wide open. Retro up top, friendly below.
gen-silkscreen-gf-noto-sans-shavian: Silkscreen draws every letter with a flat, unvarying line, pixel-bright and lo-fi, and leaves generous space around each one. Noto Sans Shavian follows in loose, rope-like curves that never knot at the ends, so a long stretch of text moves smoothly.
gen-silkscreen-gf-noto-znamenny-musical-: Terminals stop well away from the stem here, which gives Noto Znamenny Musical Notation a clean, modern look. Noto Znamenny Musical Notation sits under Silkscreen, whose cable-like strokes hold one thickness and bring the lo-fi, retro spacing.
gen-silkscreen-gf-ojuju: Ojuju has the tempered contrast of a lightly flexed spring wire, with wide s curves barely curled in. Ojuju feels approachable next to Silkscreen, whose lo-fi, retro lines hold their thickness and sit far apart.
gen-silkscreen-gf-overpass: Spaghetti-thin lines laid out in spaced letters give Silkscreen a lo-fi, retro look all its own. And Overpass keeps its strokes modern and consistent, with e shapes you would never mistake for a blot.
gen-silkscreen-gf-palanquin: Silkscreen is all retro spacing and no calligraphic swell. Palanquin brings curved letters with wide, unclosed mouths beneath it, so the lo-fi heading gets a contemporary, professional partner that feels easy to read.
gen-silkscreen-gf-philosopher: Pixel-retro up top, soft and curvy below: Silkscreen has no brush-like swelling at all, only spaced-out lo-fi letters. And Philosopher answers in a plain sans with curves full of daylight and shifts in thickness that never turn stark.
gen-silkscreen-gf-pontano-sans: Pontano Sans has wide open c terminals and a contemporary, professional feel. Pontano Sans takes the quiet role under Silkscreen, whose lo-fi lines look squeezed out like toothpaste, and sits happily at a modest size.
gen-silkscreen-gf-pt-sans: Silkscreen draws lo-fi, retro letters like toothpaste squeezed in one steady line, with space you can almost feel between them. PT Sans takes over below, approachable and professional, with c forms that read as open arcs.
gen-silkscreen-gf-quattrocento-sans: Retro pixels meet modern calm. Silkscreen is best at loud, lo-fi display lettering with thin joins no thinner than its stems, while Quattrocento Sans does its best work keeping c from looking like o.
